metadata.title: MIL-STD-3071 TMS Data Model — Topic Conformance Catalog (custom)

links.text: MIL-STD-3071 TMS Data Model IDL v2.0.2 (checked-in ground truth)

metadata.remarks: CUSTOM (non-NIST) OSCAL catalog. Controls are derived from MIL-STD-3071's A.8.7 Topic Usage classification (Required / Conditional-on-10-named-conditions / Optional) and Tables B.1/B.2 (pp.64-65), plus cross-cutting requirements from D.4 (IDL annotations)/D.5 (QoS) and A.8.6 (topic naming). Per MIL-STD-3071 §1.5 (p.1): "This document does not define test procedures that verify compliance with this standard" — no attestation/report format is prescribed anywhere in the standard, so this catalog and its assessment format are a project-defined conformance framework, not a certified DDS conformance test. Optional-usage topics (18 of the 37 topic bindings in tms-coverage.json) are intentionally NOT modeled as controls here — A.8.7 defines them as never mandatory.

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: "Required. Implemented by all TMS devices" (A.8.7, p.44). Every TMS device — regardless of role — SHALL implement these 8 topics.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The device SHALL publish Heartbeat at a 1 s period so subscribers can detect loss of on-bus liveness, independent of any other topic's cadence.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Cross-reference: docs/compliance/tms/tms-coverage.json topics[] binds `Heartbeat` to type `Heartbeat` (idl_line 3672). Section B.4.1. QoS profile: Medium (Periodic 1 s, 3 s deadline).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The device SHALL publish DeviceInfo at start-up (and make it available to late-joining subscribers via TRANSIENT_LOCAL durability) declaring its role, product identity, and the TopicInfo describing which conditional/optional topics and request topics it implements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Cross-reference: docs/compliance/tms/tms-coverage.json topics[] binds `DeviceInfo` to type `DeviceInfo` (idl_line 5286). Section B.5.1. QoS profile: PublishLast (At Start, TRANSIENT_LOCAL/RELIABLE).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The device SHALL publish ActiveDiagnosticState at start-up and on any change to its set of active diagnostic trouble codes, most-severe-first truncated at 64 entries with an overflow count for any codes beyond that.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Cross-reference: docs/compliance/tms/tms-coverage.json topics[] binds `ActiveDiagnosticState` to type `ActiveDiagnosticState` (idl_line 3215). Section B.12.1. QoS profile: PublishLast (At Start, On Change).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The device SHALL publish ActiveMicrogridControllerState at start-up and on every change of which Microgrid Controller (if any) it currently recognizes as active, per the MC-selection state machine (A.7.5).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Cross-reference: docs/compliance/tms/tms-coverage.json topics[] binds `ActiveMicrogridControllerState` to type `ActiveMicrogridControllerState` (idl_line 4539). Section B.13.1. QoS profile: PublishLast (At Start, On Change).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The device SHALL publish EnergyStartStopState (present/future start-stop level, lock, elapsed/remaining time, reason, actor) at start-up and on any level change.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Cross-reference: docs/compliance/tms/tms-coverage.json topics[] binds `EnergyStartStopState` to type `EnergyStartStopState` (idl_line 4476). Section B.16.1. QoS profile: PublishLast (At Start, On Change).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The device SHALL publish PowerPortState (per-port cable/connection/switch status) at start-up and on any change, for every power port it exposes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Cross-reference: docs/compliance/tms/tms-coverage.json topics[] binds `PowerPortState` to type `PowerPortState` (idl_line 3567). Section B.17.1. QoS profile: PublishLast (At Start, On Change).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The device SHALL publish a Reply within 0.1 s of receiving any Request-pattern topic it subscribes to, keyed on requestingDeviceId/targetDeviceId, carrying a ReplyStatus.

parts.name: statement

groups.title: Cross-Cutting Requirements (Transport, QoS/Timing, IDL Annotations D.4/D.5, Topic Naming, Value Conventions)

parts.name: overview
parts.prose: Requirements that apply across all topics rather than to one topic each — the D.4/D.5 "Conformance testing will verify..." categories (extensibility, keys, bounded values, units, QoS interoperability), the transport binding (D.1-D.3), topic naming (A.8.6), and this project's documented value-representation adaptations.

controls.title: Transport binding: DDS/XCDR2/RTPS vs. project adaptation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All OMG DDS participants SHALL use XCDR2 encoding (D.1), connect to domain ID 0 by default (D.2), and use the Chapter B topic names over DDSI-RTPS (D.3). This project does not implement DDS at all; it is a documented, honest adaptation (MQTT+JSON) — see the 'adaptation' guidance below.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: ADAPTATION: this adapter serializes each TMS struct to JSON and publishes over MQTT, never DDS/XCDR2/RTPS. This is a 100% project adaptation stated openly (docs/tms-compliance.md §7.1) — the IDL is used only as the schema-shape oracle, not as a wire-interoperability target. This control is assessed for schema-shape fidelity, not DDS interoperability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every topic SHALL use its assigned QoS profile (PublishLast/Command/Response/Reply/Continuous/Medium/Slow/Rare) with the Durability/Reliability/History/Deadline/Priority values of Table A.5. "Conformance testing will verify that devices under test interoperate with other devices using the given values" (D.5).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: MQTT has no native profile equivalent; this project approximates via QoS0/QoS1 + a publish-cadence timer per topic. Known violations tracked in docs/tms-compliance.md §9 / behavioral-findings.md (PowerHardwareUpdate/StorageUpdate over-publish vs. Slow/10 s; DeviceInfo's TRANSIENT_LOCAL/RELIABLE emulated by periodic republish; Reply published QoS0 not Reliable).

controls.title: Per-profile delivery deadline and publish-rate limiting

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Publishers SHALL update samples at the nominal rate for their topic's data trigger and SHALL NOT publish faster than the profile's rate limit (burst size 1 or 10, A.8.5.3); subscribers rely on the profile's delivery deadline (2 s Continuous / 3 s Medium / 20 s Slow / 2000 s Rare) to detect a communications fault.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tracked violations (behavioral-findings.md): PowerHardwareUpdate/StorageUpdate publish every ~2 s against a Slow/10 s profile (should rate-limit); DcMeasurementUpdate's Medium/1 s nominal isn't met by the 2 s default poll interval.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: "These annotations change the DDS serialization and must not be removed. Conformance testing will verify that devices interoperate with appendable and mutable changes" (D.4.2.1).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Not applicable in the literal DDS-XTypes sense (this project has no XCDR2 wire, so there is no extensibility-kind byte to interoperate against); the JSON binding's analogous property is additive-only field evolution in lib-schema, tracked informally, not machine-checked today.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: "Key values should not be removed entirely, as this may increase the DDS network traffic. Conformance testing will verify interoperability with devices that do use key values" (D.4.2.3).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Every @key-annotated IDL field is preserved as a Rust field in lib-schema (verified by the tms-idl-codegen descriptor-factory's byte-identity proofs, crates/lib-tms-model/tests) — tms-coverage.json's `keys` count per type is the machine-readable evidence.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: "Conformance testing will verify that devices publish values within this range, and subscribers flag out-of-range values, but not whether these annotations are used" (D.4.2.4).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: IDL @range/@min/@max annotations are captured per-field in the generated catalogue (tms-coverage.json's `ranges` count); runtime range *enforcement* on values populated by lib-mapping is not yet independently machine-tested — tracked as future work, out of this gate's current scope (it reads tms-coverage.json, not live telemetry).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: "Conformance testing will verify that device use the proper units of measurement but not whether this annotation is used" (D.4.2.5).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All @unit-annotated fields spot-checked correct against the IDL (behavioral-findings.md: "Units all spot-checked correct (p.u. SoC, degC, s, V/A/W, W/s)"); tms-coverage.json's `units` count per type is the machine-readable evidence of annotation presence in the catalogue.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: "All of these requirements can be determined from the information that is published in the device announcement (Section B.5). Conformance testing will verify that publishers and subscribers participate in topics consistent with their DeviceInfo" (A.8.7).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This adapter declares an empty TopicInfo.supportedRequestTopics (honest — no command surface), per decision 0003's supersession; the two named request topics it additionally subscribes as defense-in-depth are answered REPLY_NOT_IMPLEMENTED rather than claimed as supported.

controls.title: Topic naming convention (prefix/middle/suffix; bare CamelCase; no per-device segment)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: DDS topic names are bare CamelCase with a data-trigger suffix per Table A.6 (Info/Reply/Request/Result/State/Update) and carry no per-device segment — devices are DDS instances keyed by deviceId, not by topic name (A.8.6, D.3).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: ADAPTATION: MQTT topics are the only per-connection addressing mechanism available, so this project uses `tms/{device_id}/{snake_slug}` — a documented, reversible bridge rule (snake_slug -> CamelCase recovers the exact IDL name) — docs/tms-compliance.md §6.

controls.title: Value representation: NaN-for-unavailable, sign convention, enum wire spellings, JSON key casing

links.text: MIL-STD-3071 A.9.6.5 (float convention, ~p.50); IDL enumerator spellings (Chapter B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Unavailable float values are represented as NaN (A.9.6.5); enumerators are transmitted using their IDL spelling; the standard defines no JSON binding at all, so JSON-specific choices (key casing, null-vs-NaN rendering) are spec-silent, not spec-violations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: ADAPTATION: JSON keys are snake_case (project/Rust convention) where the IDL is camelCase — a mechanical, reversible mapping (docs/tms-compliance.md §7.2); every enum variant carries #[serde(rename = "IDL_SPELLING")] (§7.4); Seplos's charge-positive current is sign-inverted to TMS's source-positive convention (§5); fields with no Seplos source are honestly NaN, never a fabricated value.
